input_signals.name: Stable Cash R&D Flywheel
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), MA(sale, 3))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with sustained R&D intensity backed by high and stable operating cash flow earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D is more credible when it is financed by recurring operating cash generation rather than transient funding conditions. The quality leg rewards firms whose cash-flow yield is high relative to its own volatility, so the signal emphasizes durable innovation capacity rather than raw R&D spending.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ma( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), ma( sale, 3 ) ) ), rank( sub( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ), vol( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge Spend Turnover Discipline

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with sustained intangible investment, improving sales productivity, and no accompanying debt build-up earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal avoids intangible-capital turnover denominators and instead looks for commercialization through rising sales-to-assets. Subtracting the change in debt intensity emphasizes disciplined financing rather than a static low-leverage tilt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( sub( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 5 ), delta( ratio( add( coalesce( dltt, 0 ), coalesce( dlc, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Retained Funding Knowledge Surplus
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3)), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(DELTA(re, 1), at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with meaningful intangible spending that is covered by retained-earnings accumulation earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces unstable retained-earnings-to-book-equity with retained-earnings growth scaled by assets. The interaction rewards intangible investment only when internally generated profit accumulation appears sufficient to fund it, reducing exposure to externally financed intangible narratives.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with a large prior R&D stock and improving operating cash-flow margins earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Durable intangible productivity should appear after investment has had time to commercialize, not merely when current spending is high. A rising cash-flow margin provides evidence that past R&D is converting into monetizable products, pricing power, or operating efficiency.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( lag( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), 1 ), at ) ), rank( trend( ratio( oancf, sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Knowledge Surplus
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with meaningful knowledge and brand investment that is covered by operating cash flow earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the Sloan accruals leg with a direct cash-funding surplus: operating cash flow after current intangible outlays. The signal rewards intangible spend only when the firm has internal cash generation sufficient to sustain it, rather than simply crossing two known anomaly levels.

input_signals.reasoning: The first leg captures a structural tilt toward research capability rather than replacement of depreciating tangible assets. Pairing that with cash margin quality focuses on asset-light intangible productivity rather than speculative R&D intensity alone.

input_signals.reasoning: The intangible leg uses the minimum R&D intensity over time, reducing reliance on one-off spikes or reporting-status effects. The quality leg favors firms where cash economics are strengthening more than reported earnings, suggesting that the research program is supported by real cash generation rather than accrual optimism.

input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(DELTA(re, 1), at), 3), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(dltt, 0), COALESCE(dlc, 0)), at), 1))))

input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from another negative goodwill-deterioration variant and instead tests the source of intangible capital formation. Internally built R&D and brand capital are more credible when retained earnings are accumulating and debt intensity is not rising, while acquired intangible growth is treated as a lower-quality substitute.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms emphasizing internally built intangible investment over acquired intangible buildup, while generating operating cash flow in excess of current knowledge spending, earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first leg separates organic intangible formation from acquisition-related balance-sheet expansion. The quality leg is a direct self-funding test: intangible investment is more durable when current operating cash flow can absorb R&D and advertising outlays.

input_signals.reasoning: The intangible leg measures the share of reinvestment directed to intangible capability rather than depreciation replacement. input_signals.name: Organic Formation Cash Share
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3), ADD(ADD(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3), ABS(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1))), RATIO(COALESCE(dp, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose intangible formation is primarily organic rather than acquired or maintenance-related, and that also generate strong cash margins, earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the industry-rank duplicate with a share-of-formation construct rather than a simple organic-minus-acquired spread. The denominator includes acquired intangible change and depreciation, so the signal asks whether cash-generating firms are allocating their investment capacity toward internally built intangible assets rather than acquisition accounting or physical replacement.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with a meaningful and stable knowledge-spending program, backed by retained-earnings accumulation and low earnings volatility, earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the direct Sloan cash-versus-earnings leg and replaces the TS_MIN spending floor with a level-plus-stability characterization of intangible commitment. The quality condition emphasizes internally retained profitability and earnings persistence, which should make sustained intangible investment more credible.

input_signals.name: Dual-Channel Cash Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), RATIO(xad, sale))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3), VOL(RATIO(oancf, sale), 5))))

input_signals.reasoning: Leaving xad unfilled avoids turning the dual-channel leg into a non-reporter mass at zero. The quality leg now uses cash-flow margin level and volatility on the same sales scaling, matching the hypothesis that dual intangible investment is valuable when cash conversion is persistent.

input_signals.name: R&D Floor Liability Coverage

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms maintaining a durable R&D spending floor while operating cash flow comfortably covers current liabilities earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: A persistent R&D floor indicates that research capability is not a one-off spending spike. Conditioning on cash flow relative to current liabilities focuses on near-term balance-sheet quality, which is important because intangible projects are long-duration and easy to cut under liquidity stress.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( ma( ratio( oancf, lct ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.reasoning: This is not a reinvestment-mix or cash-surplus rehash; it asks whether the firm is extracting more sales from its asset base after including recent intangible outlays. The quality leg adds a cash-cycle discipline condition, requiring that intangible-adjusted sales efficiency be supported by operating cash generation.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( sale, add( at, ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ) ) ), 5 ) ), rank( ma( ratio( oancf, act ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Ranked Short-Debt Knowledge Cushion

input_signals.reasoning: The revision avoids subtracting ratios with incompatible denominators by ranking cash-margin strength and short-debt burden separately through SUMRANK.
